stage1.impression: This is a clean, symmetrical listening room: two red acrylic horn speakers on oak plinths in front of a charcoal pleated drape, with rows of identical oak chairs. It reads as CG straight away. The floor is a flat, glowing salmon plane and is the brightest thing in the frame. The pleats are perfectly regular, the plaster is a smooth gradient, the chairs are clones, and there is no visible light source and no sign of life. The speakers do carry the only saturated colour and their acrylic glows convincingly at the edges, but the horns sink into black and the room has nothing that makes it a specific place. A magazine would see a generic screening-room or showroom render, not a published photograph of this pop-up.

blocking_9: The floor and rug must sit darker than the speakers and read as real sealed concrete and wool at 1:1 (floor lum_median about 45-70 instead of 108, with visible aggregate, sheen variation and rug pile)
Remove the overall pink/red cast so that plaster, concrete and oak read neutral-warm under 2700 K, and Ember is the only saturated colour
The speakers must be the brightest objects with a legible horn silhouette (speaker region lum_median >= 45, horn not crushed)
Show at least one visible practical (a lit Core or Hemisphere) so the light reads as the room's own
Add signs of life and specificity (the decks table, a record out of its sleeve, glasses, a coat, the ceiling track) so it reads as this pop-up and not a generic room
Use a believable lens: a 28-35 mm seated or eye-level view instead of 20 mm, without a foreground chair-back block
Give the felt real fibre texture and irregular folds, and the chairs individual wear, so nothing reads as a cloned CG surface

defects.what: The floor/rug is a featureless salmon-pink plane and the brightest surface in the frame (median 108, RGB 147/100/74), with no concrete aggregate, rug pile or sheen variation
The floor colour is far from the specified #4E4943 (dE2000 17.5), with a strong red cast
The left plaster wall is bright (median 113), smooth and pink (dE 23 vs #BDB4A6), and pulls the eye to the frame edge
The right speaker's horn is almost crushed (crush 48%) and loses its silhouette against the felt
The hero speaker is darker than the floor (median 28.6, below the 45 target)
The felt drape has perfectly regular, CG-looking pleats with no fibre, lint or fold irregularity
Repeated identical chair models: the same oak grain and pose on every chair
A blurry foreground chair back fills the lower-right corner and reads as an obstruction
No visible practical, no props and no sign of life; the 20 mm lens stretches the edges (left chairs, right plinth)
The left plinth is lit as brightly as the floor (median 102) and competes with the speaker it carries

changes.problem: The floor/rug is overlit and is the brightest surface in the frame, so the room reads as a lit stage floor rather than a night room.

evidence.measured: lum_median 108.5, RGB median 147/100/74, while the speaker region is 28.6

change.setting: track spots: the seats 1 x spot, and the listening pair 2 x spot
change.from: seats 6.0 W cone 60 deg; listening pair 90.0 W cone 18 deg
change.to: seats 1.5 W cone 40 deg; listening pair 70 W, re-aimed onto the speaker cabinets and horns (not the floor in front of them), with the floor tone #4E4943 -> #3F3B36 and a little sheen variation

changes.expected: The floor drops to a dark, warm pool with soft fall-off between the rows, darker than the speakers

changes.problem: A global red/magenta cast turns plaster, concrete and oak pink, so Ember is no longer the only saturated colour.

evidence.measured: floor dE2000 17.5 vs #4E4943; plaster dE 23.3 vs #BDB4A6 (RGB 141/111/85)

change.to: 2700 K / +3.0 (toward green), so 2600-2700 K sources render warm-neutral rather than pink

changes.expected: Neutral surfaces fall within a modest warm shift of their spec colour; red is left only in the speakers

changes.problem: The hero speakers are underexposed against the floor, and the horns crush into the felt.

change.setting: soft light: the back felt's wash
change.to: 2.0 W/m2, graded brighter behind the horns, giving a dim halo that separates the horn silhouettes; plus the listening spots' aim raised so the horn lips catch a highlight

changes.expected: The horns read as a silhouette with edge highlights; the cabinet glow becomes the brightest part of the frame

changes.problem: The left plaster wall is bright, smooth and pink, and draws the eye to the frame edge.

change.setting: the plaster tone, and the room's fill
change.to: plaster #A39B8F with trowel/roughness variation, fill 0.06 W/m2

changes.expected: The side wall falls off into shadow toward the frame edge, with visible hand-trowelled texture

changes.problem: The 20 mm lens stretches the edges and the foreground chair back blocks the lower right, which reads as a wide CG view rather than a photographer's frame.

evidence.measured: a blurred chair back covers about 8% of the frame; the left chairs and the right plinth are stretched

change.to: 32 mm, seated height (1.1 m), from the aisle between the rows, toed slightly so the decks table by the drape and the ceiling track enter the frame and no chair back crosses the bottom edge

changes.expected: A believable seated listener's view, with the pair and the decks table as the subject

changes.problem: There is no sign of life or of this specific pop-up, so the frame reads as a generic screening room.

evidence.measured: empty chairs, a bare floor and no props anywhere in the frame

change.to: a record out of its sleeve leaning on a front-row chair, two glasses on the floor by chair legs, a coat over one chair back, a sleeve stack on the decks table

changes.expected: The room reads as in use between sessions; small highlights on vinyl and glass

changes.problem: No visible practical: the light has no source in the frame, so it reads as CG lighting.

evidence.measured: frame p99 169 comes only from speaker acrylic edges; no lamp in frame

change.setting: EARF's lamps: a Core on the decks table
change.to: a lit Core in frame at 1.2 W, glow 0.03, plus haze density 0.0006 -> 0.0015 so the listening spots' cones read faintly

changes.expected: A warm practical gives the light a visible origin; faint beams add atmosphere

changes.problem: The felt pleats and the chairs read as perfect CG copies: regular folds, identical grain, no fibre.

evidence.measured: evenly spaced pleat highlights across the whole drape; felt lum_median 18.9 with no fibre texture at 2x

change.setting: the felt's finish, and the oak's stain
change.from: uniform #26272A felt; one oak texture on every chair
change.to: a wool-felt fibre normal map with slight lint and colour variation within charcoal (#232427-#2B2C2F); each chair's oak texture offset or rotated, with slight stain variation

changes.expected: The drape reads as heavy wool and the chairs as individual pieces

out_of_scope.request: Vary or reduce the pleat geometry of the drapes, or move the chairs out of their perfect rows
out_of_scope.why: The plan (A-401) fixes the drapes and the chair layout; only finishes, light and props may change

out_of_scope.request: Show only one speaker so that a single hero carries the colour
out_of_scope.why: The listening room holds the fixed Tropos pair in Ember on its plinths; two speakers is the design

out_of_scope.request: Make the horn resin less dark so that it holds detail on its own
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour and parts are fixed; only light on it may change
